0.8.1 is a drop-in patch for 0.8.0: format epoch 4, the server's storage and protocol formats and the extension's formats (`USQ2`, `USS3`, `USL1`) are unchanged. 0.8.0 and 0.8.1 nodes run in one cluster during a rolling upgrade, 0.8.0 and 0.8.1 owners and readers of one stream work side by side, and owners upgrade one at a time. Upgrade in place with an ordinary rolling restart (`helm upgrade`), with no fresh install or data move. Rolling back to 0.8.0 is safe once `raft.deleted_data_max_age` (Helm `raft.deletedDataMaxAgeMs`) is unset, since 0.8.0 refuses unknown configuration keys.

- **Set `raft.deleted_data_max_age` only once every node runs 0.8.1.** It bounds how long a deleted, purged or expired stream stays in snapshots, the Raft log and old snapshot objects (Helm `raft.deletedDataMaxAgeMs`). Unset, it is the larger of 1 hour and eight times `raft.install_snapshot_timeout`. A set value must be at least eight times `raft.install_snapshot_timeout`, or the node refuses to start. A 0.8.0 node refuses the unknown key.
- **Expect a one-time drain and GC burst after the upgrade.** Once a group's leader runs 0.8.1 it removes expired streams in the background, about 4,100 a minute per group, so `stream_count` and `retained_bytes` drop within minutes and cold GC sees a burst of deletes. The first journal passes copy up to about twice a core's live log (`wal_rewritten_bytes`), and snapshot GC deletes old unused snapshot objects. While 0.8.0 and 0.8.1 nodes run together, an install can fail once with `snapshot not found` and is retried with a newer snapshot.
- **`POST /__ursula/raft/{group}/purge` can answer `503` with `Retry-After`** while a snapshot of the group builds or an earlier purge has not landed. Send it again then.
- **A restart purges the log through the restored snapshot**, and an idle group that pins old log files is purged through its snapshot, so a follower may catch up by a snapshot install rather than from the log.
- **A single node now runs the snapshot driver.** It keeps 64 entries below a snapshot instead of 1,000, builds one snapshot at a time below `raft.snapshot_log_budget`, keeps its snapshots inline and never refuses writes for its log. `storage.snapshot.drive_interval = "0s"` restores the 0.8.0 behavior.
- **A SQLite commit above `URSULA_VFS_MAX_COMMIT_BYTES` (128 MiB by default) fails as `too_large`** at its COMMIT, and SQLite rolls it back. Split larger transactions, or raise the limit (at most 1 GiB) on every host that may own the database, with memory for about three times the limit. `WriteRefusedKind` gains `too_large`.
- **A snapshot build that outlives its group engine writes nothing**, so a build left running by a node shutdown or a recovery plan's cut can no longer replace a restarted replica's snapshot pointer with an older one and leave a gap between its snapshot and its log. 0.8.0 has the same race.
- **A snapshot read whose range starts past the end answers `416`** naming the current token under any `Stream-Incarnation`, where 0.8.0 answered `412` under a retired token.

Known issues: [#411](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/411), [#461](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/461), [#465](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/465), [#496](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/496), [#517](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/517), [#518](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/518), [#539](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/539), [#561](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/561), and [#687](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/687), [#698](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/698) and [#709](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/709), which were already present in 0.8.0 and are listed for the first time. Every change is listed in the [0.8.1 release notes](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/release-notes#081).
